headline: Rain is water that has traveled from ocean to sky and back—an endless cycle
universal_truth: Nothing is truly new; everything is recycled through larger systems
fun_facts: The water falling as rain today has been cycling through Earth for billions of years
A single raindrop takes about 10 minutes to fall from cloud to ground
On average, water spends 9 days in the atmosphere before falling as precipitation
discussion_questions: What cycles do you participate in without noticing?
How does knowing rain is ancient change how you see a storm?
What would happen if the water cycle stopped?

hook.script: The rain falling today is ancient. The same water has been cycling from ocean to sky to land and back for billions of years. The drop that lands on your window might have fallen on dinosaurs, filled Roman baths, flowed through countless rivers. Nothing is wasted in nature.

cliff.script: Every day, the Sun lifts billions of tons of water from the oceans into the sky. How does liquid water become clouds, and then return as rain? What makes it fall?
cliff.prompt: What triggers rain to fall from clouds?

options.text: Water droplets combine until they're heavy enough that air can't hold them up
options.response: Yes. When droplets grow large enough, gravity overcomes air resistance and they fall.

options.text: Cold air causes water vapor to suddenly condense and fall
options.response: Cold does cause condensation, but there's more to why it falls...

fact1.title: The Water Cycle
fact1.script: Sun heats ocean water, which evaporates—becoming invisible vapor. The vapor rises, cools, and condenses into tiny droplets around dust particles. Those droplets form clouds. When enough droplets merge, they become heavy enough to fall. Rain.

fact2.title: Ancient Water
fact2.script: Earth's water is a closed system—essentially no new water is created or destroyed. The water you drink has been through countless cycles: ocean, atmosphere, glacier, river, plant, animal. You're drinking recycled dinosaur water.

fact3.title: The Journey Down
fact3.script: A raindrop falls at about 14 miles per hour and takes roughly 10 minutes to travel from cloud to ground. During that journey, it might evaporate partially, merge with other drops, or freeze and melt multiple times.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Rain reminds us that we're part of cycles larger than ourselves. The water in your body will one day be clouds, rivers, oceans. You are not separate from nature—you are nature, temporarily assembled.

outro.script: That's Day 39. Tomorrow, we'll discover what causes thunder. Until then, next time it rains, remember: you're witnessing the same water cycle that has sustained life for billions of years.

growTrack.title: Cycle Awareness - See the System
growTrack.learning_objective: Recognize the cycles you participate in
growTrack.activity: Follow water today: drink a glass and trace where it might have been—ocean, cloud, river, reservoir, tap. Then trace where it will go next. You're a waystation in an endless cycle.
